articles.title: We Tested Dozens of Women's Walking Shoes — Here are the Best Ones
articles.summary: NBC Select staffers put dozens of women's walking shoes to the test. Here are the options that came out on top from Hoka, NoBull, Saucony and more.
articles.body: If you’re not a fan of running, biking or swimming, brisk walking is one of the best ways for adults to fulfill the Center for Disease Control and Prevention’s recommended 150 minutes of moderate-intensity activity a week. Not only does it get your blood pumping, but it also offers benefits like improved sleep quality, increased bone strength, boosted energy levels and regulated blood pressure, according to the American Heart Association. And all you need is reliable walking shoes, whether you’re getting steps in outdoors or on a treadmill. To help you find a comfortable, supportive pair of women’s walking shoes, I consulted podiatrists about what to look for while shopping. I also rounded up a handful of options to consider, including expert picks and sneakers tested by the NBC Selected staff. Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter. The best women’s walking shoes of 2026 Before putting together this list, I asked podiatrists and NBC Selected staff for their recommendations. I also note which sneakers have the American Podiatric Medical Association’s Seal of Acceptance — shoes earn this stamp of approval after they’re reviewed by a group of APMA podiatrists who find them to promote good foot health. All of the sneakers on this list are available in half and whole sizes. Most of the shoes I recommend come in a variety styles, so if you’re looking for something specific, like a certain color or pattern, browse the full selections online. Remember that you’ll need to break in any shoes you buy before wearing them across long distances or for long periods of time, says Dr. Jacob Wynes, a podiatric surgeon and an associate professor of foot and ankle surgery for the University of Maryland School of Medicine. He recommends doing this by wearing them for a couple hours a day for about a week. Best overall “These are the most comfortable walking shoes I’ve tried. They make me feel like I’m walking on clouds,” says former NBC Selected editorial projects manager Rebecca Rodriguez. The shoes are made with thick, plush foam cushioning, and they’re bouncy — NBC Selected senior editor Nikki Brown compares the feel to mini trampolines or bed springs. Nike’s Motiva shoes also have a wavy-patterned outsole that helps them absorb the impact of your steps and grip the ground, according to the brand. Plus, their rocker shape propels you forward while walking. Best budget buy Ryka’s lace-up sneakers are one of the lower priced options on this list, and they don’t compromise on quality. The shoes are specifically designed around the shape of women’s feet, so Ryka gave them a narrower heel, a roomy toe box and soft cushioning in the midsole. They also have a grippy rubber outsole, arch support built into the insole and extra cushioning in the forefoot and heel. NBC Selected associate SEO reporter Ashley Morris says they soften her landings, too. “These sneakers absorb the shock from my steps really well, which is important to me since I deal with shin splints that can be irritated by too much pressure,” she says. Best cushioning Dr. Miguel Cunha, a podiatrist and founder of Gotham Footcare in New York City, recommends Hoka’s Bondi sneaker for its maximum cushioning and breathability. The midsole is made from an even layer of soft, lightweight foam, which helps diffuse impact across the feet while walking and gives the shoe its minimal heel drop. The sneaker also has an internal heel counter, a piece of supportive material in the back that stabilizes the heel and reduces your risk of getting blisters, experts say. Dr. Olga Shvets, a podiatrist at Central Park Podiatry in Yonkers, New York and Bay Ridge Family Podiatry in Brooklyn, New York, also recommends highly cushioned Hoka sneakers like these for anyone whose job requires them to stand for long periods of time, like nurses and teachers. Best for walking and running It’s rare that I find a sneaker I’m equally happy to walk and run in, but this one is cushioned and comfortable enough to support me across both types of exercise. The sneakers feel soft under my feet, are slightly springy and have plush foam that protects my joints and absorbs impact. The shoes’ curved outsole also lets me easily roll through strides, especially when I’m speed walking or jogging. Anyone can wear these sneakers, but Shvets says she specifically recommends them to her elderly clients because they have a rounded toe and grippy rubber bottom that helps prevent falls. She also likes that the insole is removable, so you can add custom orthotics if needed. Best for long distances I’ve been a fan of Brooks’ Glycerin sneakers for years and can rely on them whether I’m walking three or 10 miles. Their bouncy, nitrogen-infused foam keeps my feet comfortable for hours, and while the cushioning is on the softer side, I never feel like I’m sinking into it. There’s noticeably more cushioning in the shoe’s heel rather than its forefoot and toe, which is why it has a higher heel drop of 8 mm — I don’t mind the feeling this creates, and I appreciate that there’s more shock absorption in the heel since that’s where my foot hits the ground first while walking. Even when my feet swell in the heat or across long distances, the shoe’s upper never makes them feel squeezed or restricted due to the breathable material it’s made with. I also like the stabilizing broad base of the Glycerin 23s. Best stabilizing shoe “I always recommend these shoes because they deliver a soft heel strike and take some stress off the feet,” says Cunha. Saucony’s Guide 18s have high sidewalls and a broad platform, which stabilizes your feet and encourages them to roll through each stride, thus reducing fatigue and preventing injury, according to the brand. The sneakers are made with soft, lightweight cushioning throughout, giving you rebound with each step. They also have a padded heel collar to help secure your feet in place while walking. Best neutral shoe These sneakers are designed to support walking workouts and speed walking, according to the brand, but Brown says they’re also a dream to wear while running errands. “They’ve been comfy since the first wear — there was no dreaded break-in period,” she says. “I love that they fit snugly yet I can wiggle my toes around. I can also easily slip in and out of them without having to bend down and untie the laces.” The sneakers are made with lightweight cushioning, a padded tongue and heel, an anti-odor lining and a two-piece flexible rubber sole. The insole also has extra arch and heel support. Most versatile “When I worked at Orangetheory, I noticed that all my coworkers, trainers and members were wearing these shoes. Finally, after getting my own pair, I understood the hype,” says former NBC Selected associate reporter Bianca Alvarez. “I love using them to walk on the treadmill or outside, and I also wear them during HIIT classes, running and lifting. They’re cushioned enough to get me through cardio, but keep me stable while training.” The sneakers have a rubber outsole, a form-fitting, sock-like upper and built-in heel loop, making them easy to slip on your feet. There’s soft, lightweight cushioning in the shoe’s midsole, and you can remove its insole. Best for commuting The Transport is one of our favorite Hoka walking shoes, and Rodriguez says they’re best for commuting, running errands and walking around her neighborhood. “These sneakers are so convenient to pull on and go since they have a toggle lace closure rather than traditional laces that you tie,” she says. “They offer so much comfort and support, so I can walk in them all day without my feet feeling tired or sore.” The shoes have a firmer feel and a thick, durable rubber outsole with pronounced treads, giving you extra traction in slippery weather conditions or on uneven terrain like trails. There’s reflective details on the Transport’s upper, which is coated in a water-repellent coating. Best for all terrains “I bought these sneakers as a colorful, comfortable footwear option for a trip to Brazil, and they were the perfect choice,” says Morris. “The bottom was grippy enough to keep me upright during jungle hikes and walks on the slick, cobblestoned streets of Rio (which is quite a feat for a habitual tripper such as myself), and the shoes have a cozy, airy feel that lets me wear them all day without any aches or pains from my flat feet.” The Salomon XT-6 are slip-ons with toggle lace system, and they have a cushioned orthopedic insole, a protective toecap and an internal fit sleeve that hugs your feet. Additionally, the shoe’s outsoles are designed with deep lugs, giving you maximum traction on all surfaces. How I picked the best women’s walking shoes If you’re shopping for women’s walking shoes, experts say it’s important to prioritize the following factors, all of which I kept in mind while curating my list of recommendations. APMA Seal of Acceptance: Brands can voluntarily submit their shoes to the American Podiatric Medical Association, where they’re reviewed by a group of doctors according to specific criteria. If the doctors find that they promote foot health, the shoes earn the APMA Seal of Acceptance. That doesn’t mean shoes without the seal aren’t good for your feet — it just means brands haven’t submitted their shoes for the APMA review. I noted which sneakers on my list are APMA accepted. Material: The best material for your shoe depends on where you typically walk (like pavement, a treadmill or trails) and the weather conditions you usually walk in. For example, a breathable material like mesh is a great choice for hot climates, but leather is better for trails with rocky terrain since it’s more durable.Traction: Walking shoes should provide a good grip and stability to help you avoid injury. Choose options with rubber outsoles, which perform especially well on trails and uneven terrain, as well as on pavement and asphalt tracks, says Shvets. A shock-absorbent rubber outsole also helps alleviate the impact of each step, says Cunha.Cushioning: A shoe’s overall comfort level is largely determined by the amount of padding in its midsole, which is the area between the insole and the outsole. That padding is often made from materials like memory foam, ethyl vinyl acetate (EVA) or gel, and can minimize the impact of each step every time your foot hits the ground, says Shvets. Support: You’ll need a shoe that supports the shape of your foot to feel comfortable, so make sure you buy a sneaker that complements your arch type (high, neutral or flat), says Cunha. Also make sure that the shoe’s flex point (the point at which it bends and creases while you’re walking) matches your foot’s bending point (the area between the toes and the ball of your foot). If the shoe’s arch support and flex point are incompatible with your feet, it can cause issues like arch pain or plantar fasciitis.Insole: Look for a memory foam footbed or an EVA anti-compression insole for added comfort to support your arches, says Cunha. If you wear custom orthotics, or think you may need to invest in a pair of shoe inserts, buy sneakers that have removable insoles, says Dr. Jacob Wynes, a podiatric surgeon and an associate professor of foot and ankle surgery for the University of Maryland School of Medicine.Heel drop: Heel drop, also called offset, refers to the difference in height between the heel and toe of a shoe. It indicates the evenness of a shoe’s cushioning and is measured in millimeters — zero drop means the shoe has totally even cushioning. A uniform level of cushioning is often more comfortable for walkers who strike the ground with their heel first and roll through their step, experts say. The lower the heel drop, the less stress the shoe places on the Achilles tendon. Ideally, walking shoes should have a heel drop of no more than 8 millimeters — some of the shoes on my list are slightly higher because they’re made for high-performance walking and running. Runners need a higher heel drop than walkers because they strike the ground first with their midfoot, the ball of their foot or forward on their heel, experts told me.Weight: “On average, walking shoes are usually between 6.5 and 13 ounces,” says Cunha. “Women’s shoes are on the lower range and men’s shoes are on the upper range, but anything less than 8 ounces is considered lightweight.” Lightweight shoes are best for speed walking, walking long distances or walking for extended periods of time.Return policy and trial period: You won’t know how your feet feel in a pair of walking shoes until you use them, so familiarize yourself with a brand or retailer’s return policy and trial period. That way you know how long you have to try shoes before deciding if you’re keeping, returning or exchanging them. How to determine your foot type Your arch determines the direction and severity of the way your foot rolls or pronates. “You can identify your [foot type] by paying attention to which part of your foot hits the ground first,” says Shvets. She recommends looking at the soles of an old pair of sneakers to see where they’re worn out, as this will indicate where you’re making most of your impact and tell you whether your foot type is a pronator, supinator or neutral. Below is a more detailed description of the three types of feet. Pronator Pronating is a natural, normal movement of the feet, and it occurs when your ankles or arches roll or tip slightly inward. But if your feet roll too far inward, you’re overpronating. This gait can cause flat feet, which is when there’s little to no arch in the feet. Some people are born with flat feet, but other times it’s a result of an injury to the ligaments or tendons, causing the arch to collapse. Those who are pronators and have flat feet will see worn tread in the middle of the heel and toward the inner edge of the heel, experts told us. A shoe with a supportive sole and a firm but cushioned insole is best for overpronators, says Cunha. Supinator When your weight rolls to the outer edges of your feet, you are supinating. Supinators will see a worn tread on the outer edge of the heel and should look for added cushioning at the heels, experts say. Neutral If your foot lands on your heel and rolls forward during your stride, evenly distributing impact across the forefoot, you have a neutral gait. Those with a neutral gait will see the most wear at the heel, as well as below the first and second toe. Meet our podiatry experts At NBC Select, we work with experts who have specialized knowledge and authority based on relevant training and/or experience. We also take steps to ensure that all expert advice and recommendations are made independently and with no undisclosed financial conflicts of interest. Dr. Olga Shvets is a podiatrist at Central Park Podiatry in Yonkers, New York and Bay Ridge Family Podiatry in Brooklyn, New York.Dr. Miguel Cunha is a podiatrist and founder of Gotham Footcare in New York City.Dr. Jacob Wynes is a podiatric surgeon and an associate professor of foot and ankle surgery for the University of Maryland Medical System. Why trust NBC Selected? I’m a reporter at NBC Select who covers fitness, and I specifically write about sneakers like running shoes with arch support, carbon plate running shoes, training shoes and walking shoes. For this article, I interviewed three experts about women’s walking shoes and rounded up expert and NBC Selected staff picks. I also test dozens of sneakers throughout the year, which helps guide my recommendations. articles.title: Will Scottish football finally agree on how to fix youth development?
articles.summary: For more than 15 years, Scottish football has been asking itself what it could be doing better - now it's preparing for a forum on the future of the game.
articles.body:
When things go wrong in Scottish football, there's a running joke among supporters about what comes next: Another think tank, another summit, another grand plan.

For more than 15 years, Scottish football has been openly and publicly asking itself what it could be doing better.

In particular, how it can produce more elite players and help the national team not just qualify for major tournaments, but compete at them.

Now, the game is preparing for another attempt.

On Friday, all 42 SPFL clubs will gather in St Andrews for what the Scottish FA describes as a "critically important" forum on the future of the national game.

Leading the discussion will be the governing body's new chief football officer, Craig Mulholland, whose brief is to shape and deliver Scottish football's long-term development strategy.

Top of the agenda is talent development - and there are few within the game who dispute that there is a problem.

Too few young Scottish players are making the grade at elite level in Scotland.

Too many find their path to first-team football blocked. And increasing numbers are leaving altogether.

These concerns are not new - the same issues have come up in four major reviews and in countless recommendations since 2010.

The challenge is agreeing on a solution.

One of the key concerns now is the lack of opportunities for young Scottish players at Premiership level.

At the start of the 2016-17 season, approximately 53% of players who started in the first round of Premiership fixtures were born in Scotland.

At the start of this season, that figure had fallen to 28%.

Compare that with Norway, where home-grown players accounted for around 73% of opening-day starters in 2016 and still made up approximately 72% at the start of the current campaign.

What that decline means for Scotland is open to debate.

Either Scottish football is producing fewer players capable of competing at Premiership level, or clubs have become increasingly reluctant to hand opportunities to those coming through their academies.

Former pro youth coach, Lloyd Gaffney believes the latter is a major factor.

Youth football games for 750 children cancelled over bad behaviour

Players threatened, official headbutted and 72 red cards in week of youth football

Gaffney spent a decade working in academy football at Dundee and Dundee United before eventually leaving the game, in part due to frustrations at what he saw.

"There is a fear because clubs can't afford to get beat," he said.

"Managers don't want to lose their jobs and boards get nervous because if the team's not doing well, there are fewer bums on seats."

But if clubs won't provide an obvious first-team pathway, what is the point in having academies in the first place?

"That's exactly what I've been asking for years because there are hundreds and hundreds of kids and hundreds of parents buying into the dream," said Gaffney.

"Players might train with the first team when they're 18 or 19 and then that's it."

Increasingly, some of Scotland's brightest prospects are deciding not to wait around to find out.

This summer alone, Scotland under-16 internationals Kai Hutchison, Keir McMeekin and Boyd Fraser left Dundee United and Hearts for Everton, Manchester City and Nottingham Forest respectively.

Two of Celtic's most highly-rated academy talents, Erskine Rennie and Dara Jakiemi, have also headed south, joining Fulham and Liverpool.

A recent report by The Athletic found the number of teenage players moving from Scotland to England increased from 35 between 2012 and 2020 to 66 between 2020 and 2026.

Before the UK's departure from the European Union, English clubs were free to recruit under-18 players from across Europe.

With that route largely closed, many clubs have increasingly turned their attention to Scotland.

Former Celtic captain Scott Brown understands the attraction.

"It's hard because agents sign them up young, promise them the world and some of them will treble their money," he said.

"As a 16-year-old at a Liverpool or a Manchester City, you could be on money that almost sets you up for life."

But finances are only part of the equation.

One agent told BBC Scotland that English clubs can often offer a superior football education through better facilities, coaching, sports science and nutrition.

Former Rangers, Hearts, Motherwell and Livingston midfielder Andy Halliday believes Scottish clubs must do more to convince players to stay.

"If these players see a pathway to the first team, it'll make their decision to leave so much more difficult," he said.

He believes intervention may now be necessary, pointing to how clubs in England have to provide eight homegrown players when they submit a 25-man squad.

But as some look at ways to prevent more young players leaving, those who have left already say they have no regrets.

And many who leave are driven by a belief that England offers their best chance of fulfilling lifelong ambitions.

Seventeen-year-old Cole Hay was with Hamilton Academical since he was seven before making the switch to Sheffield United's academy.

"Ever since I was seven or eight, I wanted to play in England," he said.

"I just think there's such an attraction in playing against some of the biggest clubs and travelling all over the country.

"The facilities are incredible, so coming down just made sense. Ultimately I want to play in the Premier League, play Champions League football and play for my country."

Hay's view is echoed by many who have crossed the border. So what can Scotland do for those who want to stay?

Some believe the answer may lie overseas.

The Scottish FA's appointment of former Belgian international Sebastien Pocognoli as head coach of the national team has already demonstrated a willingness to look beyond its own borders.

Some within the game believe elements of Belgium's youth-development model could be worth exploring.

The Belgian approach places greater emphasis on technical development, small-sided games and individual decision-making at younger ages, with coaches encouraged to guide rather than instruct.

There is also greater patience with so-called "late developers", recognising that talented players do not all progress at the same speed.

Just as importantly, Belgian clubs operate with clearer pathways into senior football.

Under-23 sides compete within the professional pyramid, helping bridge the gap between academy and first-team football.

Scott Coyne of the Belgian Football Podcast believes that system gives young players more incentive to stay, but it requires "patience and a unified coaching philosophy across the game".

"Clubs have to treat academies as part of the core business, not side projects," he added.

Others believe different solutions are required.

Football analyst John Walker has suggested a financial reward system designed to incentivise clubs to play young players.

Under his proposal, clubs could receive payments ranging from hundreds of pounds per start in the Premiership down to smaller amounts further down the pyramid.

Walker argues the money could be reinvested in coaching, infrastructure and experienced players while still creating opportunities for young talent.

How Scottish FA used AI in selecting new Scotland boss Pocognoli

Youthful Pocognoli the brave choice for Scotland job

Former Hearts midfielder Ryan Stevenson would go further still.

He wants reserve league football reintroduced to bridge what many see as a crucial development gap between youth and first-team football.

At present there is no dedicated elite age-group competition for players aged 19 to 21 in Scotland.

Stevenson believes regular matches against experienced professionals, fringe first-team players and those returning from injury would better prepare young players for the demands of senior football.

Recent initiatives have attempted to address the issue.

Premiership clubs have entered B teams into competitions, introduced co-operation agreements and expanded loan arrangements.

Data suggests those measures have helped increase playing time for under-21 players below Premiership level.

One chief executive believes agents should be required to register with the Scottish FA before operating in Scotland, allowing greater scrutiny of approaches to players under the age of 16.

Others want the governing body to lobby Fifa for changes to the international compensation model.

Celtic received a modest development fee when the teenager joined Liverpool after only a handful of first-team appearances.

A few years later, Liverpool reportedly sold him for around £25m.

For many clubs, that highlights the growing imbalance in the market for young talent.

Whether the answer is quotas, incentives, reserve football, coaching reform, agent regulation or changes to compensation rules, Scottish football is unlikely to leave St Andrews united on every issue.

But there is growing agreement on one thing.

If Scotland is to continue qualifying for major tournaments and begin making deeper runs at them, the next generation and this summit matters.

articles.title: Juiz da Colômbia suspende bombardeios contra crianças guerrilheiras | G1
articles.standfirst: Ataques aéreos contra grupos guerrilheiros foram retomados após Abelardo de la Espriella se tornar presidente.
articles.summary: Ataques aéreos contra grupos guerrilheiros foram retomados após Abelardo de la Espriella se tornar presidente.
articles.body:
Abelardo De La Espriella presta continência após tomar posse como novo presidente do país durante a cerimônia de posse, em Cali, Colômbia, em 7 de agosto de 2026 — Foto: REUTERS/Luisa Gonzalez

Um juiz da Colômbia determinou, nesta quinta-feira (3), que o governo do presidente direitista Abelardo de la Espriella suspenda os bombardeios militares contra acampamentos da guerrilha quando houver informação sobre a presença de menores recrutados.

Apoiado pelo presidente americano, Donald Trump, o novo chefe de Estado colombiano, que chegou ao poder em 7 de agosto, impõe a linha-dura no enfrentamento das máfias do narcotráfico, com bombardeios letais contra guerrilheiros.

A ordem judicial se aplica ao departamento amazônico de Guaviare, onde De la Espriella ordenou recentemente dois ataques aéreos que mataram ao menos 33 dissidentes da extinta guerrilha das Farc.

No último domingo, a autoridade forense informou que entre os mortos na primeira operação havia três menores entre 15 e 16 anos. Ainda não se sabe se havia menores entre as vítimas do mais recente.

Um tribunal da cidade de San José del Guaviare ordenou "a suspensão temporária" dos bombardeios contra acampamentos de grupos armados "quando houver informação de inteligência" ou outros alertas sobre "a possível presença de crianças e adolescentes".

A medida cautelar, à qual a AFP teve acesso, estará vigente enquanto o juiz analisar um recurso judicial apresentado por um cidadão contra o governo e as Forças Militares pela suposta violação dos direitos fundamentais dos menores.

O governo enfrenta duras críticas de parte da oposição e de organizações de defesa dos direitos humanos.

"Sabemos que é preciso submeter estes grupos armados. Mas a pergunta é: o que fazemos com estas crianças?", questionou o cientista político e estudante de direito Roxemhberg Rozo, de 35 anos, que apresentou o recurso legal.

"A resposta governamental não pode ser bombardeá-los e matá-los", disse.

De la Espriella expressou, na última segunda-feira, seu apoio a estes bombardeios contra "os bandidos que durante décadas recrutaram menores para transformá-los em combatentes ou em escudos humanos".

O Ministério da Defesa argumentou que a operação cumpriu com "todos os padrões legais".

O presidente é alvo de várias críticas por ter divulgado um vídeo no qual comemora um dos bombardeios, enquanto caminha em meio a cerca de 20 corpos de guerrilheiros mortos , cobertos por lençóis brancos.

A morte de menores em bombardeios militares também ocorreu durante os governos do esquerdista Gustavo Petro (2022-2026) e do direitista Iván Duque (2018-2022).

Um dos ministros da Defesa de Duque renunciou, pressionado por moções de censura no Congresso por causa destas operações.

No ano passado, foram registrados 428 casos de recrutamento de menores por parte de grupos armados, segundo a Defensoria do Povo. Do início deste ano até 31 de julho, foram 97.

articles.title: Kalil defende investimentos em polos econômicos de Minas Gerais | G1
articles.standfirst: Candidato do PDT visitou o Porto Seco de Varginha nesta quinta-feira (3) e falou sobre desenvolvimento regional. Depois, seguiu para Uberaba, no Triângulo Mineiro.
articles.summary: O candidato Alexandre Kalil visitou Varginha e Uberaba para discutir o desenvolvimento regional e o fortalecimento dos polos econômicos de Minas Gerais.
articles.body:
Kalil defende investimentos e fortalecimento de polos econômicos em Minas — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

O candidato do PDT ao governo de Minas Gerais, Alexandre Kalil, teve compromissos de campanha no Sul do estado nesta quinta-feira (3).

O primeiro compromisso foi no Porto Seco de Varginha, um dos principais centros logísticos da região. Kalil estava acompanhado de políticos, empresários e assessores.

Em uma reunião com diretores do empreendimento, o candidato ao governo falou sobre investimentos, gestão fiscal e também da importância do Sul de Minas para o desenvolvimento de outras áreas do estado.

“A região é o exemplo do desenvolvimento mineiro, né? É o orgulho do desenvolvimento mineiro. Eu considero três grandes polos: a Região Metropolitana, o Triângulo Mineiro e o Sul de Minas. Então, nós precisamos aproveitar isso”, afirmou.

Após o encontro, Kalil seguiu para a sede da EPTV, afiliada da Globo no Sul de Minas, onde participou de uma entrevista de 30 minutos. Ele respondeu a perguntas sobre as propostas do seu plano de governo.

articles.title: Apple é processada nos EUA por patentes usadas em iPhones | G1
articles.standfirst: Empresa química BASF diz que dona dos iPhones usa sua tecnologia contra falhas em sistemas de reconhecimento facial em vários celulares e tablets.
articles.summary: Empresa química BASF diz que dona dos iPhones usa sua tecnologia contra falhas em sistemas de reconhecimento facial em vários celulares e tablets.
articles.body:
Modelos da linha iPhone 17 em loja da Apple nos EUA, em foto de 19 de setembro de 2025 — Foto: Reuters/Shannon Stapleton

A Apple foi processada nesta quinta-feira (3) pela empresa química alemã BASF sob a acusação de infringir a tecnologia patenteada de autenticação facial usada em vários modelos de iPhone e iPad.

Em sua denúncia, a trinamiX, subsidiária da BASF, afirma ter passado a última década desenvolvendo tecnologia para solucionar falhas em sistemas convencionais de reconhecimento facial que permitem fazer o desbloqueio facial usando fotografias, máscaras impressas em 3D e réplicas de silicone.

A denúncia diz que a Apple não usou a tecnologia patenteada da BASF quando lançou o Face ID, seu recurso de autenticação facial, em 2017 com o iPhone X. Mas aponta que a fabricante agora a utiliza em vários produtos, incluindo o iPhone 15, iPhone 16, iPhone 17 e iPad Pro.

"A Apple sabia, ou deveria saber, da alta probabilidade de que a atualização de seus iPhones e iPads para incorporar o Face ID usando detecção de material e pele" infringisse sete patentes da trinamiX, ​​causando "danos substanciais e prejuízos irreparáveis", diz a queixa.

O processo será analisado pelo Tribunal Distrital dos EUA em Midland, Texas, e busca indenização por danos não especificados e a suspensão de novas violações.

A Apple não respondeu imediatamente aos pedidos de comentários.

A dona do iPhone vendeu US$ 196,5 bilhões em iPhones (cerca de R$ 1 trilhão) e US$ 21,7 bilhões em iPads (R$ 110 bilhões) entre o quarto trimestre de 2025 e o segundo trimestre de 2026.

Segundo a BASF, a origem da trinamiX remonta a 2010, quando cientistas que pesquisavam células solares orgânicas fizeram descobertas inesperadas que levaram à construção dos primeiros protótipos de câmeras tridimensionais.

A BASF criou a subsidiária em 2014 como uma entidade independente para desenvolver tecnologias avançadas de sensoriamento 3D e de materiais.

A trinamiX detém mais de 800 patentes concedidas ou pendentes em todo o mundo, segundo a denúncia.

articles.summary: Em Montes Claros, o candidato Gabriel Azevedo defendeu a criação de um corredor ferroviário ligando o Norte de Minas à Bahia para impulsionar a economia regional.
articles.body:
Gabriel Azevedo visita Norte de Minas e propõe corredor ferroviário para escoamento da produção — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

O candidato do MDB ao governo de Minas Gerais, Gabriel Azevedo, cumpriu agenda de campanha em Montes Claros, no Norte do estado, nesta quinta-feira (3).

Pela manhã, ele participou de uma sabatina na Inter TV Grande Minas, afiliada da Globo, e apresentou propostas para áreas como saúde, educação e segurança hídrica em regiões afetadas pela seca.

Gabriel também defendeu a ampliação da malha ferroviária do estado. O candidato, que se apresentou como “governador das ferrovias”, propõe a criação de 15 corredores ferroviários, entre eles um ligando Corinto, Montes Claros e Janaúba, em Minas Gerais, a Caetité, na Bahia.

Segundo Gabriel, a proposta tem como objetivos reduzir custos com fertilizantes, facilitar o escoamento da produção e aumentar a competitividade dos produtos.

“Primeiro, que a gente reduz o custo dos fertilizantes. Segundo, a gente tem a melhora do escoamento. O produto fica mais competitivo, mais dinheiro para o empresário, mais dinheiro pro trabalhador, mais dinheiro no bolso das pessoas. Terceiro, diminui a quantidade de caminhão [nas estradas]. Você que é caminhoneiro, não fica preocupado com o emprego não, porque o caminhão continua importante para levar até o trem e depois até a outra ponta”, afirmou.

Durante a sabatina, o candidato também falou sobre o combate à violência contra as mulheres e defendeu uma atuação preventiva do estado para reduzir os feminicídios.

Após a entrevista, Gabriel seguiu para um tradicional café da cidade acompanhado da candidata a vice-governadora, Maria Helena de Quadros Lopes, e da equipe de campanha. No local, cumprimentou eleitores.

Depois, a comitiva foi a um restaurante, onde o candidato se reuniu com empresários e lideranças políticas.

No fim da tarde, Gabriel deixou Montes Claros e seguiu para Belo Horizonte, onde tinha outros compromissos com veículos de imprensa.

articles.title: CHS: Seconci troca presidente e vice após denúncias em Sorocaba | G1
articles.standfirst: Mudança ocorre nesta quinta-feira (3) e atinge os dois principais cargos de comando da organização social que administra o hospital, que atende 48 municípios da região.
articles.summary: O Seconci substituiu a presidência do Conjunto Hospitalar de Sorocaba após o Ministério Público apontar graves falhas estruturais e falta de profissionais na unidade.
articles.body:
O Serviço Social da Construção Civil do Estado de São Paulo (Seconci), organização social que administra o Conjunto Hospitalar de Sorocaba (SP), trocou nesta quinta-feira (3) os dois cargos de comando da entidade: a presidência e a vice-presidência.

Há duas semanas, a Secretaria Estadual da Saúde já havia pedido o afastamento de três profissionais do Seconci : o responsável técnico pelo CHS, o gerente de relações institucionais e o gerente administrativo-financeiro.

A mudança informada nesta quinta-feira ocorre após denúncias de irregularidades na administração do hospital, que atende 48 municípios de toda a região.

Conjunto Hospitalar de Sorocaba (CHS) é referência em captação de órgãos — Foto: Reprodução/TV TEM

Segundo o Seconci, no lugar da presidente Maristela Honda entra o médico Haruo Ishikawa. Já no lugar do vice-presidente José Antonio Marcondes Cesar assume Antonio Carlos Salgueiro de Araújo. Haruo Ishikawa já havia ocupado o cargo antes de Maristela.

Conforme a organização social, a mudança foi feita após uma reunião do conselho deliberativo.

"Nós ouvimos alguns servidores do conjunto que relataram problemas, especialmente deficiências nas equipes de enfermagem, nas equipes de limpezas, problemas estruturais, principalmente nos elevadores e na climatização do prédio. E na verdade essas informações corroboraram com informações que já tínhamos, acompanhando com órgãos de fiscalização, como Conselho Regional de Enfermagem (Coren), Conselho Regional de Fisioterapia e Terapia Ocupacional (Crefito) e Cremesp, que apontam as irregularidades e com isso, passamos a cobrar providências do Seconci e da Secretária de Estado."

O representante do MP-SP também comentou sobre a sobrecarga relatada pela equipe ouvida.

"Há evidentes prejuízos, servidores relatando que em muitas vezes tem que escolher entre uma função e outra, entre dar banho pro paciente ou dar medicamento pro paciente, porque não dá pra fazer tudo dentro do horário. E isso, evidentemente, causa prejuízo no atendimento à população. Além disso, os servidores trabalhando sobrecarregados, isso aumenta a pressão, aumenta o risco adversos pros pacientes, sem dúvida nenhuma."

Anteriormente, a Comissão Especial de Monitoramento da Rede Estadual de Saúde da Câmara apresentou o relatório final sobre o Conjunto Hospitalar de Sorocaba . O documento de 155 páginas reuniu denúncias de mortes, sobrecarga de trabalho, falhas estruturais e inconsistências financeiras no hospital, que é gerido por uma Organização Social (OS).

articles.title: Trump nomeia secretário interino para o Exército dos EUA após crise | G1
articles.standfirst: Adam Telle substitui Dan Driscoll, que pediu demissão após meses de tensão com Pete Hegseth, secretário da Guerra de Trump.
articles.summary: Adam Telle substitui Dan Driscoll, que pediu demissão após meses de tensão com Pete Hegseth.
articles.body:
Adam Telle foi anunciado por Trump como secretário interino do Exército dos EUA — Foto: Michael Brochstein/Sipa USA/Reuters

O presidente dos Estados Unidos , Donald Trump , anunciou nesta quinta-feira (3) que está nomeando Adam Telle como secretário interino do Exército dos EUA. Telle ocupa atualmente o cargo de secretário assistente do Exército para obras civis.

"Adam Telle é um grande patriota, respeitado por todos", afirmou o presidente em um post na sua rede social Truth Social.

Na segunda-feira (31), a imprensa americana reportou que o então secretário do Exército, Dan Driscoll, havia pedido demissão, após meses de tensão com o chefe do Pentágono , Pete Hegseth.

Telle atua no Gabinete de Obras Civis do Exército desde agosto de 2025, segundo o Legistorm, site que monitora legisladores e assessores do Congresso americano. Antes disso, Telle passou 20 anos trabalhando principalmente no Congresso para legisladores, inclusive como chefe de gabinete do senador republicano Bill Haggerty, do Tennessee, entre 2021 e 2025.

Ele trabalhou por 18 meses na Casa Branca durante o primeiro mandato de Trump, atuando como assistente especial do presidente para assuntos legislativos , informou o Legistorm, e também trabalhou por mais de 10 anos para o falecido senador republicano Thad Cochran, do Mississippi.

O militar vai supervisionar a maior força de combate do país em um momento em que os EUA ainda estão envolvidos em conflito com o Irã e forças significativas do Exército estão estacionadas no Oriente Médio.

O Secretário do Exército, Dan Driscoll, presta depoimento durante uma audiência no Senado americano em maio de 2026. — Foto: Nathan Posner/Reuters

Segundo a imprensa americana, Driscoll e Hegseth entraram em atritos frequentes desde que o segundo assumiu o cargo, em janeiro de 2025. O secretário de Guerra é aliado do presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump.

A tensão entre Driscoll e Hegseth teria resultado na demissão do chefe do Estado-Maior do Exército, general Randy George, em abril.

Driscoll e George eram parceiros próximos, segundo o jornal "The Wall Street Journal", e desenvolviam juntos projetos de renovação tecnológica no Exército. Os dois também viajaram juntos para a Ucrânia antes da demissão do general.

A remoção de George provocou críticas a Hegseth entre deputados e senadores do próprio partido, os republicanos.

Em comunicado enviado ao WSJ, a Casa Branca elogiou o trabalho de Driscoll. A porta-voz Anna Kelly afirmou que o secretário foi eficaz na implementação da agenda de Trump, na preparação das Forças Armadas para operações militares e nas negociações entre Rússia e Ucrânia.

O secretário de Defesa dos Estados Unidos, Pete Hegseth, fala durante uma declaração à imprensa ao chegar para uma reunião de ministros da defesa da OTAN na sede da organização em Bruxelas, quinta-feira, 18 de junho de 2026. — Foto: AP Photo/Virginia Mayo

Hegseth chegou a servir no Exército dos EUA e atuou no Iraque e no Afeganistão, mas fez carreira como âncora do canal de TV conservador Fox News antes de ser indicado por Trump para comandar o Pentágono.

A chegada de Hegseth à chefia do Departamento de Guerra foi vista com desconfiança pela liderança militar dos EUA, composta em grande parte por funcionários de carreira.

No primeiro semestre de 2026, o secretário passou a promover uma "limpa" na alta cúpula das Forças Armadas. Uma reformulação militar ampla é incomum na história do país, ainda mais em momentos de conflito aberto, como a guerra contra o Irã.

Durante a tarde, ele fez uma visita ao Porto de Cabedelo e concedeu uma entrevista. Na sequência, ele também fez visitas no Bairro de Intermares, também em Cabedelo.

articles.summary: Após ablação cardíaca em São Paulo, a prefeita Emília Corrêa recebeu alta e segue em repouso em um hotel, conforme orientações da equipe médica.
articles.body:
Emília Corrêa, prefeita de Aracaju — Foto: PMA/Divulgação

A prefeita de Aracaju , Emília Corrêa, informou nas redes sociais que recebeu alta hospitalar nesta quinta-feira (3), após ser submetida a uma ablação cardíaca. O procedimento foi realizado na tarde da última terça-feira, na cidade de São Paulo.

"Queria dizer que já recebi alta do hospital, eu estou agora no hotel onde eu vou seguir repouso, por recomendação médica. Foi tudo bem", disse Emília.

A ablação é um procedimento considerado minimamente invasivo e não exige cortes cirúrgicos. Os médicos inserem cateteres — pequenos tubos flexíveis — através dos vasos sanguíneos até alcançarem o interior do coração.

No local, a equipe identifica o ponto exato que provoca a alteração nos batimentos e elimina a arritmia utilizando energia, normalmente por radiofrequência.

articles.title: HelloFresh Meal Delivery Review: What to Know Before Subscribing
articles.summary: I tried HelloFresh’s meal kits for a week to help make cooking at home easier and stress-free. Here’s what I thought about the service’s meals and pre-measured ingredients.
articles.body: I come from a long line of great cooks, which makes my lack of kitchen skills quite disappointing. My mom and grandma were both pros at making intricate, delicious meals throughout my childhood, yet I never inherited their expertise — even when I have a recipe written out in front of me, the meals usually turn out undercooked, underseasoned or not quite right. In the years spent living away from them I’ve put more effort into making food that will actually taste good. But like with any skill, practice makes perfect, and what better way to improve than by getting pre-measured ingredients and detailed recipes delivered to my door? I decided to give HelloFresh a try for one week, and it completely changed my outlook on cooking and saved me trips to the grocery store. Below, I outline my experience with the meal delivery service, including what to know about pricing, preparation and meal selection. What is HelloFresh? HelloFresh is a meal delivery service that sends you fresh, pre-measured ingredients to your doorstep so you can make a (preselected) recipe of choice. Each week, you’ll choose meals from a rotating menu (that changes weekly) and the service will send a box of recipe cards and the exact ingredients to make your selected portion size. Nothing in the box comes frozen or needs to go in the freezer, though I personally like to freeze any meat that I won’t be cooking in the next few days. All of the included ingredients are considered grocery-store fresh. There are six dietary preferences to choose from: meat and veggies, veggie (there are 14 vegetarian meals, including two vegan meals, on the menu each week), family-friendly, fit and wholesome, pescatarian and under 20 minutes. Though your preferences won’t influence the menu options for the week, they do ensure that those meals show up at the top of the list, which is great if you have specific dietary restrictions. You can choose your desired meals at least five days before your next scheduled delivery, or you’ll automatically receive pre-selected meals that fall under your specific preferences each week. You can filter meals to show pork-free and vegetarian options on the menu, change or swap proteins and sides, or add a protein to a vegetarian dish. In addition to cooking your meals, you’ll need to do some light prep work, including chopping, slicing and mixing. How much does HelloFresh cost? HelloFresh starts at $9.99 per serving and has a $10.99 shipping cost per week. There are 15 total weekly plans to choose from; for each plan, you’ll need to choose the number of people you’re feeding (two, four or six) and the number of meals you want, ranging from two meals to six meals per week. Two-person plan: Two meals ($45.96), three meals ($59.96), four meals ($79.92), five meals ($99.90), six meals ($119.88)Four-person plan: Two meals ($79.92), three meals ($119.88), four meals ($159.84), five meals ($199.80), six meals ($239.76)Six-person plan: Two meals ($119.88), three meals ($179.82), four meals ($239.76), five meals ($299.70), six meals ($359.74) How I tried HelloFresh To try out the service, HelloFresh sent me three meals that I chose from its weekly rotating menu: Saucy Turkey Burrito BowlsOne-Pan Cheesy Chicken Tortilla MeltsCreamy Lemon Spinach Ricotta Ravioli I received my meals on a Thursday and tried them over the course of one week. I prepared and cooked the meals myself based on the directions on the recipe card, which denotes which ingredients and how much of them to use (with pictures) along with cooking and prep instructions. This was especially helpful when multiple recipes used the same type of pepper or cheese, for example. I split the meals with my partner; the portion size for each option was perfect for two people, and I often had enough meals for three dinners. The menu has more than 60 varied meal options to choose from, and since neither one of us has dietary restrictions, choosing meals was easy and straightforward. My experience with HelloFresh meal kit delivery From selecting meals to preparing and eating them, my experience with HelloFresh was mostly smooth and easy. Below are some key takeaways after trying the meal kit delivery service for a week. Choosing meals The meal selection process is very straightforward: You’re given a menu of more than 45 meals for a specific week, and you can choose a variety of dinner options like mandarin chili organic chicken and chicken Caesar wraps, and even brunch choices like peaches and cream French toast. However, the meals are tame and fairly predictable, so if you’re an adventurous eater or a true foodie, this service likely isn’t for you. The service has as many as 60 meals on its weekly menu. I’m not a picky eater, nor do I have any restrictions or special eating habits, so I had plenty to choose from due to the sheer number of options that HelloFresh offers. However, keep in mind that HelloFresh does not cater to most dietary restrictions outside of vegetarian and pescatarian diets, including gluten-free, allergen-free, keto and paleo diets. Seeing the full recipe certainly helped with the selection process. I love that I can click on a meal while browsing the menu and see the exact recipe card, including ingredients, cooking instructions and detailed nutritional information like allergens, calories, cholesterol and sugar. It was helpful for me to see standout ingredients, consider time and cooking difficulty, and survey how the meal could help me meet any specific protein and calorie goals I had for the day. The service lets you see the menus for the next six weeks, whether you’re a subscriber or not. Not only did this help me see whether HelloFresh was a good fit for my dietary needs and preferences, but it also helped me plan your meal choices ahead. Packaging and delivery The meal kits come in an insulated, lunchbox-like container with an extra-large ice pack that keeps everything cool and fresh. Most of the ingredients for each meal (with the exception of larger packages like meats and pastas) are packaged inside of a labeled paper bag, so I didn’t have to guess which ingredients pair with what meals. I found that the ingredients held up very well during delivery, and the packaging was protective enough to help meat, sauces and other potentially messy foods arrive safely with no spillage. I was genuinely surprised at how well the ingredients stayed fresh because the delivery itself was not easy. For my area, UPS delivered my HelloFresh meal kits. I live in a walk-up building with no mail room or front desk, so if I’m at work or away from my apartment during the week, packages don’t get delivered. It took three separate tries to get the meal kit delivered to my apartment (though I can’t hold HelloFresh entirely responsible for this. The brand likely does not control the delivery process once it leaves its shipping facilities and it’s something I’ve experienced with other meal delivery services I’ve tried in the past. Plus, many of them don’t hold up as well as HelloFresh. Fortunately, the contents were not impacted by the delivery delay. My order was shipped just a few days after I chose my meals and my (expected) delivery was later that same week. Ingredients Admittedly, the freshness of the ingredients surprised me. I didn’t have very high expectations about the quality of the ingredients since they’re being shipped out rather than bought directly from a store, and delivery was tough. However, they arrived in near perfect condition, as if I had gotten them directly from my local store just minutes before. Plus, as I noted above, ingredients come neatly packaged in a labeled paper bag for each meal, so all ingredients were easy to find for a specific recipe. And unlike other meal kits I’ve tried in the past, all of the ingredients I needed were actually included (and even some extras). One of my favorite aspects about meal kits in general is that the ingredients are proportioned, so you’ll almost always get the exact amount you need. That means no more wasting food, which is especially helpful considering that I have a habit of buying too much of a certain item, and then feeling guilty about throwing it away when it goes bad. With that in mind, certain foods like produce and bread will spoil fairly quickly, so I worked quickly to cook meals within the week after delivery (or else I would risk losing a few ingredients). Cooking and preparation I was initially intimidated by the fact that there’s cooking and prep work involved for all meals (generally, I prefer prepared meal delivery services that save time and energy). However, that concern disappeared when I actually got started. In general, HelloFresh is not for you if you’re unwilling or unable to follow directions for basic cooking tasks, like handling raw meat, cooking and broiling foods in an oven, using a stove top and searing meat. Fortunately, I found all of those tasks easy to do with the help of the included recipe cards. For my specific meals, they had clear instructions for draining any juices and how to add the included spices to raw meat prior to cooking it. All of the meals I tried were beginner-friendly (which, as a non-cook, is key for me). Plus, each meal I chose for the week took less than an hour to make, and two of the three were ready in under 30 minutes. Each recipe card also lists a difficulty level — easy, medium or hard — so I knew immediately how much effort I’d need. Overall, the meals looked great and tasted even better. The directions were easy to follow, so I never found myself struggling to prepare a meal, and no part of the cooking process was too difficult for me to do even as someone who does not cook regularly. It was also a great learning opportunity — I managed to practice skills, like flipping a fully loaded tortilla and caramelizing onions, that can only get better with time. How does HelloFresh compare to other meal kit delivery services? I’ve tried several meal kits and pre-made meal delivery services over the course of the past three years — most are hit or miss. HelloFresh is one of the better meal kits I’ve tried because the ingredients are fresh, it’s great for beginners and the meal options are varied and delicious. At $9.99 per serving, HelloFresh is comparable to many popular meal kits, including Blue Apron ($9.49) and Home Chef ($9.99). The $10.99 shipping cost for all deliveries is also comparable to those competitors, which range from $10.99 to $13.99 depending on plan size. The HelloFresh base prices are generally more affordable to other meal kit delivery services with more options for dietary restrictions, including Purple Carrot ($11) and Sunbasket (anywhere from $11.49 to $24.49), however its menu isn’t as extensive or inclusive of different diets. Who is HelloFresh best for? HelloFresh is great for those with busy schedules who hope to take the guesswork out of scheduling and preparing meals for the week. Depending on where you live, it may even help you save money in the long run since you can skip on overbuying food at the grocery store, according to experts in our guide to meal kit delivery. HelloFresh also provides a good amount of flexibility and lets you make changes to your delivery as needed: When you log into your account, you can update your food preferences, the number of recipes you want to receive per week or the number of people you’re cooking for. You can also seamlessly adjust the delivery date online or skip a delivery. The service has a diverse enough mix of dishes in its weekly rotating menu and can support families or groups of up to six people. You also have the flexibility to choose between two and six meals per week so you can order just enough based on your work or travel schedule. What makes HelloFresh work for most people is that the recipes are easy to follow and very beginner-friendly, so experienced chefs and non-cooks alike can make a great meal. If you are new to the culinary world (like me), it also gives you the opportunity to practice and perfect basic skills in the kitchen. Why trust NBC Selected? I am an updates editor at NBC Selected and have been covering and reviewing meal delivery services for the past three years, including prepared meals, gluten-free and vegetarian meal delivery. I tried HelloFresh meal kit delivery for a week and considered the quality of the meals, delivery and packaging, cooking instructions and more. articles.title: Couple Found Dead by Kids Near Hot Tub While on Vacation Remembered as New Details About Investigation Emerge
articles.summary: The deaths of Thomasina and Patrick Tobin in Spain have “left an immeasurable void,” an online notice read
articles.body:
A Sept. 3 online notice announced that Patrick and Thomasina Tobin died on Aug. 24 while on vacation in Spain

The couple's bodies were discovered by their children near a hot tub, and investigators continue to look into what led to the tragedy

"Thomasina and Paddy will be deeply missed by their children, their families, relatives and many friends," the notice read

The married couple who were found dead by their teenage children near a hot tub at a Spanish rental property while on vacation are being remembered as the investigation into their deaths continues.

A notice announcing the Aug. 24 deaths of Patrick, of Ireland, and Thomasina Tobin , who was originally from New Zealand, was posted online on Thursday, Sept. 3.

"Thomasina and Paddy will be deeply missed by their children, their families, relatives and many friends," the notice read in part about the couple.

"Thomasina and Paddy shared a life filled with love, family and friendship," the notice later read. "Their sudden passing has left an immeasurable void in the lives of all who knew and loved them."

Thomasina was a quantity surveyor, and Patrick worked at global technology company HCLTech in London, The New Zealand Herald reported .

A previous statement shared with PEOPLE from Spain's Civil Guard said that Thomasina and Patrick were found dead in the coastal town of Cullera, in Valencia.

The couple's two children, who are reportedly in their teens, found the bodies, the Civil Guard previously said.

In an earlier statement to PEOPLE, a spokesperson for Ireland's Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade said that the department was "aware of this case and is providing consular assistance."

A New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade spokesperson shared a statement with PEOPLE on Friday, Aug. 28, that read, "We are aware of the death of a New Zealander in Spain. For privacy reasons, no further information will be provided."

Meanwhile, as reported by Spanish outlet Levante-EMV, investigators believe the hot tub's water circulation system might have contributed to the Tobins' deaths.

Initial autopsy results from the Valencia Institute of Legal Medicine indicated that suction entrapment — in which the drain of a swimming pool or hot tub sucks in a person's hair or jewelry, resulting in possible drowning or major injuries — could be a factor in the tragedy.

Local police said the couple had a "cardiopulmonary incident due to acute stress" and ruled out drowning, according to Levante-EMV .

Never miss a story — sign up for PEOPLE's free daily newsletter to stay up-to-date on the best of what PEOPLE has to offer, from celebrity news to compelling human interest stories.

Spanish outlet Las Provincias previously reported that investigators were working to determine whether a combination of mechanical failure of the hot tub, electrocution and toxic fumes might have contributed to the deaths.

PEOPLE contacted Spain's Civil Guard and the Valencia Institute of Legal Medicine on Thursday, but did not receive immediate replies.

Meanwhile, Thursday's death notice for the Tobins stated that the funeral arrangements would be announced in due time.

"May they rest in eternal peace together," the notice read.

articles.title: In 1988, Doris Day bought a 1929 California hotel; she turned it into one of America's best-known pet-friendly retreats
articles.summary: US News: When Doris Day became a co-owner of the Cypress Inn in Carmel-by-the-Sea in 1988, she was not simply investing in a historic California hotel. The Hol.
articles.body: When Doris Day became a co-owner of the Cypress Inn in Carmel-by-the-Sea in 1988, she was not simply investing in a historic California hotel. The Hollywood star and lifelong animal advocate saw an opportunity to create a place where people could travel without leaving their pets behind. Built in 1929 in the Spanish Colonial Revival style, the hotel already had a distinctive character when Day and local businessman Dennis LeVett became its owners. One of the biggest changes under its new management would be welcoming guests’ dogs. The Cypress Inn's own history now credits Day's vision with helping transform the property into one of America's best-known pet-friendly boutique hotels. More than three decades later, the hotel continues to carry the imprint of the actress whose second act became deeply connected with animal welfare.Doris Day and the 1929 Cypress Inn hotel in CaliforniaThe building that became Cypress Inn had already been standing for nearly six decades when Doris Day entered its story. The hotel was constructed in 1929 in Carmel, California, in the Spanish Colonial Revival style, a design that gave it the distinctive character it retains today. In its own history of the property, Cypress Inn says the building originally opened as Hotel La Ribera before later becoming Cypress West. By the mid-1980s, Day and local businessman Dennis LeVett had become co-owners. The Los Angeles Times, reporting on the new ownership in March 1988, described the hotel as a historic property and highlighted the arrival of a very different kind of guest policy, dogs would be welcome. The decision reflected Day's long-standing affection for animals and would eventually become central to the hotel's identity.How Doris Day turned the California hotel into a pet-friendly retreatFor Doris Day, making Cypress Inn pet-friendly was closely tied to her own relationship with animals. The hotel's account of her legacy says her vision was to create a welcoming escape where guests and their four-legged companions could be treated equally. The idea was unusual enough in the 1980s to distinguish Cypress Inn from conventional hotels, where travelling with a dog could be difficult. The Los Angeles Times captured that change soon after Day's arrival, reporting that guests' dogs would be welcomed under the new management and observing that Day could hardly have chosen another policy given her passion for animals. Over time, the concept became more than a rule at the hotel. It became its defining character, helping establish Cypress Inn as a destination specifically associated with pet-friendly hospitality in Carmel-by-the-Sea.Doris Day's animal advocacy shaped the Cypress Inn legacyThe Cypress Inn was only one part of Doris Day's commitment to animals. After her Hollywood career, she devoted much of her later life to animal welfare and established organisations including the Doris Day Animal Foundation and Doris Day Animal League. The Cypress Inn says her work focused on rescuing, healing and finding homes for animals, particularly those that were often overlooked. That philosophy naturally found an expression at the hotel, where animals were not treated as an inconvenience to human travellers but welcomed as part of the experience. The hotel's history describes Day's involvement as helping create a place where elegance and compassion could coexist. Her influence therefore extended beyond the practical decision to allow pets inside a hotel. She helped give pet-friendly travel a distinctive identity at Cypress Inn, turning her personal love of animals into part of the property's public character.Why Cypress Inn remains one of America's best-known pet-friendly hotelsMore than 30 years after Doris Day became a co-owner, Cypress Inn continues to preserve the vision that made the property unusual in the first place. The hotel describes itself as one of the country's most iconic boutique hotels and says Day's influence remains visible in its approach to guests and their pets. Its history traces the property from its 1929 origins through its transformation under Day and LeVett into a pioneering pet-friendly hotel. The significance of the story is not simply that a famous actress owned a historic California hotel. It is that Day used the property to make an idea, that people should not have to leave beloved pets behind when travelling, part of the hotel's identity. Today, Cypress Inn remains a living piece of her legacy, combining its historic Carmel setting with the pet-friendly philosophy that she helped establish decades ago.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: France records ‘hottest summer ever’ in 2026
articles.summary: France joins other European countries in recording its hottest summer since measurements began.
articles.body:
France has recorded its hottest summer ever in 2026, joining Belgium, Britain and Ireland as temperatures soar in Europe, the globe’s fastest-warming continent.

“We have just lived through the hottest summer ever recorded since measurements began in 1900,” French Environment Minister Monique Barbut said on Thursday at a presentation of the summer climate report.

France has endured multiple severe heatwaves this year, including one in late June that set a new intensity record.

The country saw an unprecedented 2,025 excess deaths recorded during the heatwave, with a particular increase in deaths among people aged over 45, said French Health Minister Stephanie Rist.

Another heatwave stretched from late July into August, matching a 23-day record previously set in 1983.

During this time, France was hit by several major wildfires, even in normally cooler and wetter regions.

According to the national weather agency Meteo France, the summer was marked by very low rainfall, with a deficit of nearly 40 percent, making it the second driest since records began.

Meteo France said the summer of 2026 recorded an average temperature of 24 degrees Celsius (75 degrees Fahrenheit), which is 3.6C (6.5F) above the normal average.

“The summer of 2026 will go down in history,” Barbut said.

“The question we must now ask ourselves is how it will be remembered … As the first in a long series of summers that continue to break records. Or as a moment when we rose to the challenge of adaptation and mitigation,” by reducing greenhouse gas emissions, she added.

Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu tasked Barbut in late July with presenting new measures to speed up implementation of France’s national climate change adaptation plan.

On Thursday, she promised conclusions “by the end of September”, including a five-year funding plan.

Millions in France, Italy, Spain, the United Kingdom and elsewhere in Europe experienced extreme temperatures this summer.

Europe is the world’s fastest-warming continent, with temperatures increasing at twice the speed as the global average since the 1980s, according to the European Union’s Copernicus Climate Change Service.
